kevin: Quick note from the late-night perf run: host-side tokenization + parse is contributing a visible p95 tail on short chats (~10% of overall tail).
alyssa: any stacks or numbers?
kevin: main hotspots: parse_request -> chunk_reassemble -> tokenize_stream -> utf8_normalize. median host parse ~0.85ms, p95 ~1.9ms on 64-token median workload.
ben: did kernel selector change? we recently flipped adaptive kernel binning.
kevin: yes, when sequences in a minibatch vary widely selector sometimes chooses fallback kernel, causing CPU churn. variance within batch jumped from 2.3 -> 6.8 in traces where tail spiked.
alyssa: coalescer could be merging different request types. We also saw smallwrites on http/1.1 causing extra parse passes. grpc p95 is ~1.3ms vs http1 ~2.4ms in same window.
ben: KV cache metrics show a small miss uptick (~1.8%) concurrent with the spikes; I suspect merged streams cause extra kvcache lookup volume and occasional evictions.
kevin: quick wins proposed: 1) add ascii-fastpath in tokenize_stream to skip utf8_normalize for ascii-only payloads; 2) make coalescer respect a seq-length bucket and avoid mixing >x stddev; 3) clamp variance before kernel decision to ignore extreme outliers.
alyssa: + for http1, enable header-fragment coalescing at ingress to reduce smallwrite reparses.
ben: microbench results: ascii-fastpath saves ~0.2ms median per small request and drops p95 by ~25% in harness. coalescer bucketing reduced mixed-batch incidence by 68% in sim.
kevin: risks: pre-reserve buffers reduce syscalls but increase per-worker RSS; will add per-worker cap and slab recycle window. also watch kvcache hotness when affinity is introduced.
deploy-bot: ticket PERF-7800 created: "host parse tail & kernel selector mismatch" assigned to kevin,alyssa,ben.
alyssa: plan: land ascii-fastpath + buffer cap today behind flags, then coalescer bucket + selector-clamp as toggle in a week. canary at 10% then measure kernel_mispredict_rate and host_parse_p95.
kevin: thanks. I'll attach short traces and a tiny flame for the team.
ben: will instrument kvcache per-batch lookup budget metric too.
alyssa: if we get host_parse_p95 under 1.2ms for small requests we probably recover ~7% of tail.
kevin: copy. proceeding.
